answers.brief_reasoning: Moth color varies and is heritable. Birds that hunt by sight eat more of the moths that stand out against the bark. Moths that match the bark survive and reproduce more, so their color alleles become more common in later generations.
answers.final_answer: Camouflaged moths survive bird predation better (68% vs about 30%) and leave more offspring. Because color is heritable, the matching color becomes more frequent in the population over generations. This is natural selection.
